rules.S (mapping): configs/stall/class_mapping.json: issue_pc_shift = 1 instruction, evidence calibrated: the cycle in which an instruction issues is compared on the pc 16 bytes behind it (the pc the warp holds next; a taken branch's on its fall-through pc).
rules.T (ledger): For the control interval that follows the issue (cycle t) of a branch instance to which the taken-branch envelope E of control.branch applies: the first H cycles (t+1 .. t+H) are booked on the branch's own code address + 16 under control:branch_fallthrough; the next R cycles on the pc of the next instruction to issue (the target) under control:branch; the cycles after that up to t + E (exclusive) there under control:branch_refetch; cycles of that interval beyond t + E (a longer stall or another floor) there under control_floor. H = fallthrough_hold_cycles = 4 and R = resolve_cycles = 3, new fields of the control.branch leaf (both devices, source placement.<device>.v1; statistics only). The stall-field split of today no longer applies to branch intervals. Mapping: control:branch_fallthrough -> wait (calibrated), control:branch -> branch_resolving (as today), control:branch_refetch -> no_instruction (calibrated).
rules.D (ledger): The async_group_wait interval of a waiting DEPBAR-class instance is booked on the code address of the warp's next instance behind it (unchanged when there is none).
rules.B (ledger): The cta_barrier interval armed by a BAR instance whose operation class contains DEFER_BLOCKING is booked on the first instance j behind the BAR in the warp's stream (at most 64 instances ahead; none found: the last one looked at) that stops the warp: stop(j) = not pass(j) and dist(j) >= Dmin, with dist(first instance behind the BAR) = the BAR's stall field and dist(j+1) = dist(j) + max(1, stall field of j). pass(j): the instance's template is served by one of the units alu_smsp, fmaheavy_smsp, fma_smsp, uniform_smsp and takes no MIO turn (return_interval_cycles = 0 and sm_service_interval_cycles = 0); measured for IMAD, FADD, FFMA, UIADD3, CS2R, VOTE, SHF, LOP3, ISETP, IADD3, VIADD (issued) and S2R, S2UR, LDS, SHFL.BFLY, MUFU, NOP, LDC, LDCU, STS, BAR, BRA (stop), structural for every other kind. Dmin and UMOV from placement_basic v2: Dmin = the smallest measured d at which the S2R carries the barrier (6 if d = 3, 4, 5 all issue); if UMOV is measured to stop, UMOV is not a pass kind (operation class root UMOV excluded by name, recorded as measured). Every other BAR form: unchanged.
rules.M (ledger names + mapping): A next-issue floor set by the service result of an instance of class MEMBAR* or FENCE*, or by the MEMBAR.ALL.CTA / proxy-fence drain, that binds beyond the instruction's stall field is named control:membar:<operation class> / control:fence:<operation class> (the stall-field part stays control_floor, as for control:yield). Mapping: ^control:membar:MEMBAR\.SC\.GPU -> membar (calibrated: s.membar_gl), ^control:membar:MEMBAR\.ALL\.CTA -> long_scoreboard (calibrated: placement_basic fence cells, the FENCE's pc beyond the MEMBAR's stall), ^control:fence:FENCE\.VIEW\.ASYNC -> long_scoreboard (calibrated: s.fence_bar, the BAR's pc), any other control:membar / control:fence -> membar (hypothesis).
rules.F (ledger): A suspended:descriptor_visibility interval is booked on the warp's next instance to issue (as suspended:sleep), not on the suspending instruction.
rules.P (converter): Poll fold (cpp/capture/poll_folding.cpp and its Python mirror), conditions for folding unchanged. Of a foldable sequence the first folded poll survives instead of the final ready poll: kept are that poll and the records behind it up to and including its reader (the first record, at most 4 behind it, whose control word's wait mask contains the poll's write barrier; none: only the poll); dropped are the records behind the reader through the final ready poll inclusive and, when the reader is a branch with a static target, the records behind the final poll up to (not including) the first record at that target, provided they are at most 16 and all of the fold's side-effect-free kinds. The surviving poll does not carry the failed after_ready fact of its own record (it stands for the sequence's wait; the engine resolves readiness). dropped_polls counts the dropped poll records. Global-sync poll folding is unchanged.

decision: Per rule and device. A criterion fails because the engine or converter does not do what the rule says: corrected, rebuilt, replayed, stated in the addenda. A criterion fails although the rule is implemented as written: that rule is taken out again (S: the mapping key; T, D, B, M, F: the ledger keying / names revert; P: the fold reverts) and the addenda say so; the other rules stay if their criteria and K6 pass without it.
hypotheses_full_gpu: Stated before the run, not criteria (full-mio4: attribution / site / per-pc 0.362 / 0.267 / 0.783 h100, 0.354 / 0.304 / 1.057 b300; per-pc error inside mbarrier-poll sites 23.3 / 54.3 points, CTA-barrier sites 10.6 / 12.1, DEPBAR sites 5.9 / 5.4): the per-pc error falls mainly in these three site kinds; the site error and the class totals move little except long_scoreboard on fence sites (control_floor -> wait today); cycles change only through P and may move either way.
not_installed_here: The 1.96 microsecond try_wait time-out and the out-of-line path beyond it; the fence's result as a dependency barrier of the instructions behind it (the replay holds the warp); the cp.async completion time; BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING as issue of the pass kinds before the wait (the replay issues them after it; only the booking moves); the scheduler; warpgroup / tensor waits (stage MMA).

addenda.when: 2026-11-20, before any implementation or replay (no data of a changed engine, converter or mapping exists)
addenda.text: Rule P, resume point made explicit for both code layouts. The inline poll's reader is a branch either to the continuation (taken when the phase is complete, the retry loop is its fall-through: u.pollcute) or to an out-of-line retry loop (taken when the poll failed, the continuation is its fall-through and the loop jumps back to it: compiled CuTe code). The records dropped behind the final ready poll therefore run up to (not including) the first record whose pc is the reader's static branch target OR the reader's pc + 16, whichever comes first, under the same bound (at most 16 records, all of the fold's side-effect-free kinds); when neither pc is reached within the bound nothing behind the final poll is dropped. Everything else of P and every criterion are unchanged.

Rule M, one mapping rule added (it is needed for K4 to be decidable on s.fence_bar.w4, where the replay books unit:fence_view_async_sm on the FENCE's pc): ^unit:fence -> long_scoreboard, evidence hypothesis; the existing ^unit:(membar|fence) -> membar keeps only ^unit:membar. Reason: no placement_basic fence cell has a single hardware sample of class membar (0 / 1 / 8 stores, 1 and 4 warps, both devices); the hardware classes on a FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S pc are wait and long_scoreboard, and which of the two a wait for the fence unit would be is not measured (hence hypothesis). Rules, values and criteria otherwise unchanged.

addenda.when: 2026-11-20, before any implementation or replay: hand check of every rule against the probe listings and the hardware tables (it should have preceded the freeze); three points made precise, no criterion changed
addenda.text: (1) Rule M, mapping: ^control:membar:MEMBAR\.SC\.CTA -> wait, evidence calibrated (s.membar_cta, both devices: the 11 cycles behind MEMBAR.SC.CTA are class wait, no membar sample; listed under data seen). Without it the catch-all would map that floor to membar and contradict K4's own s.membar_cta clause. (2) Rule F as worded (the next instance) cannot meet K4 on the first copy of s.fence_bar, where two VIADD sit between the fence and the BAR.SYNC that carries the hardware's long_scoreboard. The control words say why: FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S writes a dependency barrier and the BAR.SYNC has it in its wait mask, the VIADD do not. Rule F therefore reads: a suspended:descriptor_visibility interval is booked on the first instance behind the suspending one (at most 16 ahead) whose control word's wait mask contains the suspending instruction's write barrier; none: on the next instance to issue. (3) Rule P: the surviving first poll carries the after_ready mask of the sequence's final ready poll (the outcome of the wait it stands for), so the engine treats it as it treats the surviving poll today; every other operand fact is its own.

addenda.when: 2026-11-20, before any implementation or replay: the two open values of rule B from placement_basic v2
addenda.text: UMOV is measured to stop the warp on both devices: operation classes with root UMOV are not pass kinds. Dmin: rule B's wording (the smallest measured d at which the S2R carries the barrier) did not foresee a split; the barrier is partly on the S2R at d = 4 (30 % / 29 %) and mostly on it from d = 5 (h100 57 %, b300 100 %). Dmin = 5 on both devices = the smallest d at which more than half of the barrier is on the S2R; a single distance cannot reproduce the split at 4 and 5, which is reported, not modelled. K3 does not depend on this choice in the d4 / d5 cells (both pcs carry at least 2 cycles of hardware barrier there). Leaf: synchronization.cta.release defer_stop_distance_cycles = 5 (statistics only; absent or 0 = the booking of today).

addenda.when: 2026-11-20, before any implementation or replay: rule P walked through the two traced record layouts (u.handoff: retries at the poll's own pc; u.pollcute: retries in an out-of-line loop)
addenda.text: (a) Same-address sequences. When the final ready poll has the same code address as the first folded poll (u.handoff, s.mbar_*: the retry is the instruction itself) only that poll survives: nothing behind it is kept from the first attempt and the records behind the final poll follow unchanged, so the stream is the one a run without failed polls has. The keep-through-the-reader and resume clauses apply only when the two code addresses differ. (b) In the resume clause a record whose execution mask is empty counts as side-effect-free whatever its kind (the predicated-off NANOSLEEP.SYNCS and PHASECHK behind a ready hint-form TRYWAIT). Criteria unchanged.

Per cell (pc x class before -> now, floor): v.nop 0.215 -> 0.132 (0.117), v.nop.w4 / .w8 / .w16 0.24 -> 0.15-0.16 (0.17-0.24), the eight v.yield1 / v.yield2 cells without .s1 0.21-0.28 -> 0.17-0.25, v.yield1.s1 1.227 -> 1.191 (0.106). The rules S and T do in these cells what they say (per taken branch 4 on the fall-through pc, 3 + 2 on the target); what remains is outside them: behind a YIELD the hardware's 45 cycles are branch_resolving 41 + misc 2 + no_instruction 2 with 2-3 of selected where the replay has branch_resolving 45, and in v.yield1.s1 (YIELD with stall 1) the hardware books them two instructions further on (39 on the ISETP behind VIADD and NOP). The threshold 0.250 was frozen from the source mean without looking at its cells; with v.yield1.s1 alone contributing 0.10 it could not be met by S and T. It stays recorded as failed. K3: FAIL in 24 of 28 cells because rule B never applied: the job's operation class of every BAR form is `BAR` (the converter's class is the opcode root), so `contains DEFER_BLOCKING` is never true; the booking stayed where it was. K7 fails through the same four cells (sync_basic-v4 class error 0.15 -> 367). Elsewhere the class error per source fell: sync_basic 0.413 -> 0.229, branch_basic 0.178 -> 0.078, mio_basic-r3 0.051 -> 0.027, mem_basic 0.388 -> 0.335, plan_pilot-r2 0.288 -> 0.267.
